bridge.usage:
Usage:
  branch-bridge [serve] [--pair] [--port 7777] [--host 0.0.0.0] [--name NAME] [--dir PATH]
                [--relay wss://relay.example.com] [--relay-only]
    --relay       Register with the relay over an outbound connection so it can be reached behind NAT (E2E encryption kept)
    --relay-only  Accept connections only through the relay, without opening a direct port
  branch-bridge pair            (same as serve --pair)
  branch-bridge devices         List paired devices
  branch-bridge unpair <id|all> Unpair devices
bridge.unpairMissing: Specify a device id or all to unpair.
bridge.relayScheme: The relay address must start with ws:// or wss://.
bridge.insecureRelay: Warning: the relay uses ws://. On public networks, use wss:// (the payload is E2E encrypted).
bridge.relayNotYet: Could not connect to the relay yet. Retrying in the background.
bridge.scanHint: In the app, go to Settings → Remote Bridge → Start pairing, then scan the QR below or paste the link.
bridge.codeLine: Or enter the address + code: code {code}  (valid for 5 minutes, single use)
bridge.checkFingerprint: Check that the bridge fingerprint shown in the app matches the one above.
bridge.noDevicesPair: No paired devices. Start pairing with the --pair option.

relay.bridgeHint: bridge: branch-bridge --relay <this address>   · For public deployments, put it behind a TLS (wss://) proxy.
